page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-1xCPU-8GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU mapped to an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates a highly polarized performance profile. The single shared core delivers strong single-core performance in Geekbench, scoring 2228.0, and average performance in gzip compression and text processing. However, multi-core and sustained throughput tests, such as stress-ng, PassMark CPU, and Redis SET operations, fall into the bottom 10% category. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds measured at 16.01 GB/sec and 13.83 GB/sec respectively.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server represents a budget-oriented tier. It offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio qualitatively suitable for memory-sensitive but compute-light applications. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU model, which limits sustained multi-threaded performance and database throughput, as evidenced by the low PassMark database score of 653.28.

This configuration is best suited for lightweight, non-compute-intensive workloads that require a larger memory footprint than typical entry-level servers. Appropriate use cases include basic text processing, single-threaded scripting, lightweight web serving, and development or testing environments where CPU resource contention is acceptable.
